problem: Next year's OKRs already show progress
what_we_found: 118 of 162 OKRs for 2027 start after the export date, yet are marked Done, Blocked, In Progress and so on.
why_it_matters: Mixed in with this year, they would distort the picture of current delivery.
what_we_did: The report opens on 2026 and shows later years separately, as plans. Ask the OKR owner what these statuses mean.
technical_detail: Rows start after the 04 Nov 2026 export yet show progress statuses (Blocked: 26, Done: 22, In Progress: 21, At Risk: 17, On Track: 17). Cycles affected: 2027: 118.
technical_treatment: Default the report to cycle 2026 and show later cycles separately. Keep all rows.

what_we_found: 184 issues were created, updated or finished after the date the file was exported, which cannot have happened yet.
why_it_matters: We cannot measure how long work takes or when it was finished.
what_we_did: Kept and flagged. No 'time to finish' measure is built. In 2026 only the finish date is affected; ask whether it is filled in automatically with the planned end date.
technical_detail: 36 of 37 resolution dates, 15 updated and 169 created dates are after the export. Affected rows by cycle: 2026: 15, 2027: 169.
technical_treatment: Flag and keep; build no cycle-time KPIs.

problem: Issues updated before they were created
what_we_found: 154 issues, all in 2027, have a last-updated date earlier than their created date.
why_it_matters: The update dates cannot be trusted for those years. Jira's updated date is also a copy of the OKR file's, so it cannot be used to double-check it.
what_we_did: 'Not updated in 90+ days' is shown only for 2026. Ask how the export produces these dates.
technical_detail: By cycle: 2027: 154. The Jira updated date equals the OKR last-update date on 311 of 311 matched rows.
technical_treatment: Publish freshness only for cycles without this problem (2026) and label it as one source.

what_we_found: 8 grades are exactly 110, and 6 of them are on work that is not finished.
why_it_matters: If 100 is the top of the scale these are probably errors, and they push averages up.
what_we_did: Kept. The main average leaves them out and the average with them is shown beside it. Ask the OKR owner whether grades above 100 are allowed.
technical_detail: All 8 are exactly 110. 6 of 8 are not marked Done (Not Started: 2, In Progress: 1, Blocked: 1, Behind: 1, At Risk: 1).
technical_treatment: Report averages with and without them, and explain the exclusion wherever the shift is material.

what_we_found: 20 finished OKRs have a grade under 50, and 57 OKRs that have not started have 50 or more.
why_it_matters: Finished OKRs average 48.3 and not-started ones 54.5, so a grade does not show how far along the work is.
what_we_did: Both are shown and never combined. Grades are labelled 'indicative'. The owner should define what a grade means.
technical_detail: Average grade by status group: Done 48.3, not started 54.5.
technical_treatment: Show both signals; list conflicts for owner review; define whether Done requires a minimum grade.

problem: Grades do not match the Key Result numbers
what_we_found: Each Key Result has a start, current and target value. For 69 of 107, the progress those numbers imply is more than 20 points away from the grade.
why_it_matters: Grades cannot be checked or recalculated from the numbers. Also, 23 have a target that points the wrong way, such as a goal to reduce something with a target above where it started.
what_we_did: The grade is used as given, with a note that it cannot be checked. The OKR tool should validate these fields when they are entered.
examples: Correlation of implied progress with grade: -0.02
technical_detail: Correlation -0.02. Also: 0 with start equal to target, 22 Decrease with a target above the start, 1 Increase with a target below the start, 24 Boolean with a non-binary target, 1 mixing % and plain numbers.
technical_treatment: Keep the reported grade as the measure and add entry validation to the OKR tool.

what_we_found: 7 OKRs and 8 Jira issues have a blank or dummy parent.
why_it_matters: Without a parent, an item cannot be counted under the objective it belongs to.
what_we_did: OKR parents were filled in from the file's indentation, which matched every one of the 304 links we could check. They are marked 'inferred' for owners to confirm. Jira parents are not used in the report.
technical_detail: OKR: placeholder: 4, blank: 3. Jira: placeholder: 8. 0 OKR links could not be inferred.
technical_treatment: Infer from indentation (agrees with 304 of 304 valid links); store in a separate flagged column.

what_we_found: Not found in this run.
what_we_did: The latest row is kept. The others are saved to okr_duplicates.csv for review.
technical_detail: Not found in this run.
technical_treatment: Keep the most recently updated row.

what_we_found: 8 OKRs and 7 Jira issues name more than one team, such as 'Digital Channels,Data Platforms'.
why_it_matters: Read as written, this looks like an extra team, and the real teams lose these items.
what_we_did: Each item is shown under every team it names. Totals still count it once, so team figures do not add up to the total.
technical_detail: OKR: 8, Jira: 7.
technical_treatment: Split with a bridge table; totals count each OKR once.

problem: One Jira key used for different issues
what_we_found: 1 key is used on 4 different issues.
why_it_matters: Linking the files by this key would attach work to the wrong goal.
what_we_did: The files are linked by the OKR key instead, which is unique. 3 keys were corrected using the usual pattern (DEMO-n belongs to X-n), and flagged.
technical_detail: 1 key shared across 4 rows with different OKR keys. 3 repaired, 0 unresolved. 2 child links depend on a repaired key.
technical_treatment: Restore the issue key from the pairing only while it holds on at least 95% of issues.

problem: Jira and the OKR file disagree on status
what_we_found: 4 of 311 linked items, most often Jira 'Done' vs OKR 'Alignment'.
why_it_matters: The share of finished work depends on which file you ask.
what_we_did: The report uses the OKR status. The disagreements are listed for owners to fix.
technical_detail: Most common: Jira 'Done' vs OKR 'Alignment': 2, Jira 'Done' vs OKR 'In Progress': 1, Jira 'Done' vs OKR 'Behind': 1.
technical_treatment: Use the OKR status for OKR KPIs; track the conflict rate on every refresh.

what_we_found: 9 of 46 finished Jira issues have no finish date.
why_it_matters: We cannot tell when that work was completed.
what_we_did: Still counted as Done, and flagged. No date is made up.
technical_detail: Status Done with a blank resolution date.
technical_treatment: Keep as Done; do not impute a date.

what_we_found: 9 Jira issues and 4 OKRs end before they start.
why_it_matters: Overdue counts and durations would be wrong.
what_we_did: Where Jira's end date is blank or differs, the OKR due date is used, and flagged. Items that still end before they start are left out of overdue counts only.
technical_detail: Jira differs from the OKR due date on 5 rows and is blank on 5 more.
technical_treatment: Use the OKR due date where Jira is blank or differs; exclude dates that stay impossible from overdue counts.

what_we_found: 32 issues have no link to any OKR; all are tasks labelled 'ad-hoc'.
why_it_matters: This work is invisible in OKR reporting, so teams look less busy than they are, and nobody can see whether it serves a goal.
what_we_did: Shown as its own group, not forced into a match. It is one of the report's five KPIs.
technical_detail: Types: Task: 32. Labels: ad-hoc: 32.
technical_treatment: Keep as an explicit Unaligned category; report its share by team.

problem: Jira points to an OKR that is not in the file
what_we_found: Not found in this run.
what_we_did: Reported as 'Jira only' with this reason. The owner should correct the key.
technical_detail: Not found in this run.
technical_treatment: Report as Jira only; owner corrects the key.

what_we_found: 19 dates are written differently from the rest of their column, such as 31.03.2026. Month names also vary: Apr, Aug, Dez, Feb, Jan, Juli.
why_it_matters: A standard date reader can silently blank these dates or mix up day and month.
what_we_did: One reader handles every format. If a date cannot be read, the run stops and names it.
technical_detail: OKR formats: text month: 974, dd.mm.yyyy: 7. Jira target dates: ISO: 669, dd.mm.yyyy: 6, text month: 6, blank: 5.
technical_treatment: Single parser for every format; stop the run on an unreadable filled date.

what_we_found: 16 OKRs have no Jira issue; all of them are top-level company objectives.
why_it_matters: Expected for the top level, which is not tracked in Jira.
what_we_did: Reported as 'OKR only'.
technical_detail: 16 are the 'ERSTE GROUP OBJ.' tier, 0 are other tiers.
technical_treatment: Treat the 'ERSTE GROUP OBJ.' tier as expected; review any other tier.

what_we_found: 12 OKRs and 10 Jira issues have no owner.
why_it_matters: Nobody is responsible for acting on them.
what_we_did: Shown as 'Unassigned' so the team lead can pick them up.
technical_detail: OKR: 12, Jira: 10.
technical_treatment: Show as Unassigned; route to the group lead.

problem: No team on a Jira issue
what_we_found: 3 Jira issues have no team.
why_it_matters: They would drop out of every team view.
what_we_did: The team is copied from the linked OKR, and flagged.
technical_detail: Blank Group column.
technical_treatment: Backfill from the linked OKR, flagged.

what_we_found: 17 rows have extra spaces or different capitals, such as 'in progress '.
why_it_matters: One status would show up as two in the charts.
what_we_did: Spaces and capitals are tidied up. The original text is kept.
technical_detail: Case and spacing variants.
technical_treatment: Trim and normalise; keep the raw value.

what_we_found: Weight is filled in on only 46 of 327 OKRs, and two other columns are completely empty.
why_it_matters: A weighted average would rest on too few weights to be fair.
what_we_did: Simple averages are used, and the report says so. Weights on Key Results should be made mandatory.
examples: Weight filled on 46, comment date on 0, hierarchy grade on 0
technical_detail: Weight filled on 46, comment date on 0, hierarchy grade on 0.
technical_treatment: Use simple averages and state the limitation.
